# SPD-061 — Bash hook: a zsh short if, while or until with a [[ ]] condition hides its body

## Brief
zsh's SHORT_LOOPS also give if, while and until a body with no then/do, and when the condition is a [[ ... ]] test the hook reads the whole line as one simple command whose command word is [[, so the body's git verb, spud call or command word is never checked (Law 7, Laws 5 and 6). SPD-042 fixed the for, select and repeat forms; this is the same hole in the sibling forms, and the ticket named them out of scope on the belief that they were read today. They are not. zsh runs them; bash 3.2 rejects each.

Evidence: Probed zsh 5.9 -f and -o nobareglobqual in the scratchpad with a fake git first on PATH: 'if [[ -n x ]] git push' pushed once; 'n=0; while [[ $((n++)) -lt 2 ]] git push' and the same with a { git push } body pushed twice; 'n=0; until [[ $((n++)) -ge 2 ]] git push' pushed twice. bash 3.2 gave a syntax error for each. On SPD-042's branch analyse_command records findings=[] for all four (the redirect target is still captured, the verb is not). The forms that do work today: 'if (( 1 )) git push' and 'while (( n < 2 )) git push' are read, because (( )) splits into subshell frames; 'if true git push' and 'if true; git push' are zsh parse errors, so only the [[ ]] spelling leaks. Fix sketch: in ShellWalk, let ']]' end an if/while/until condition the way SPD-042's end_header ends a loop header, then reuse resolve_body and close_sublists.

## Size, persona and model decision
Batch plan v2 of 2026-09-15, after the SPD-065 package split: the eleven remaining hook tickets on one worktree (spd-061-hook-batch), in three waves, because bin/spudlib/shell/analyse.py, directories.py and bash_rule.py are the hub every shell ticket touches and parallel members share one working tree. Wave 1, member 1 of 2: SPD-061 with SPD-059 and SPD-060, one engineer on opus, no children, owning shell/walk.py, zsh.py, analyse.py, syntax.py, expansions.py and tests/test_hooks.py. SPD-061 is walk.py: let ]] end an if/while/until condition the way SPD-042's end_header ends a loop header.
